task.title: Keep remote message deletion pending until durable storage completes
task.classification: remote runtime storage persistence and user-data deletion

coreClaim: Deleting a message through the remote web runtime no longer reports a false failure at the browser's 30-second deadline while the server-side deletion is still running.
rootCause: The specialized chat_messages_bulk_delete wrapper used the default finite remote request deadline even though it starts a durable, non-idempotent deletion. Slow Pi storage could continue the server transaction after the browser aborted at 30 seconds, causing the UI to report failure and roll back its optimistic cache state.

inScope: Single-message, bulk-message, and game or scene cleanup callers that share the wrapper
Live Pi diagnosis and exact-image post-merge deployment proof
outOfScope: Changing Rust deletion semantics or storage persistence
Changing confirmation prompts or message regeneration behavior
Removing the default finite deadline from reads or ordinary commands
Deleting or repairing existing user data

claimBoundary.coreClaim: The specialized durable message-deletion command may explicitly opt out of the browser's internal request deadline without changing its command name, payload, or embedded behavior.
claimBoundary.riskType: remote-runtime deletion completion, false failure reporting, and cache consistency
currentPathsOrFormats: Remote web shell using the hostable De-Koi runtime
Embedded Tauri shell using the same typed chat command wrapper
Existing chat_messages_bulk_delete payload with chatId and messageIds
legacyPathsOrFormats: Embedded Tauri IPC continues to use its existing invoke behavior.
Remote reads and ordinary commands retain the default finite deadline.
outOfScopeClaims: This change does not guarantee deletion completes within a fixed duration.
This change does not accelerate slow disk or storage transactions.
This change does not retry deletion or claim success before the server responds.
This change does not alter which messages are selected for deletion.

contractLaneGate.brokenContract: A client deadline treated an unfinished durable deletion as failed even though the server transaction continued and could still commit.
contractLaneGate.consumer: Single-message deletion, bulk deletion, and game or scene cleanup flows
contractLaneGate.impliedContract: A durable, non-idempotent deletion must remain pending until the runtime reports its real result when aborting the browser request cannot roll back the server-side transaction.
contractLaneGate.actualEnforcement: bulkDeleteMessages passes { timeoutMs: null } to invokeTauri, reusing the existing remote request option that omits the internal timer while still waiting for the runtime's real success or error response.
contractLaneGate.primaryOwnerDetail: The focused shared API wrapper owns the transport policy for this specialized durable command across embedded and remote runtimes.
contractLaneGate.wrongLaneFixToAvoid: Do not suppress the UI error, add an automatic retry, or fake success: the original transaction may still commit, so retrying can race the same destructive operation.
regressionProof: pnpm exec vitest run src/shared/api/chat-command-api.spec.ts src/shared/api/storage-api.spec.ts

positiveRows.claim: The specialized bulk message deletion command opts out of the internal remote deadline.
positiveRows.evidence: The focused wrapper regression asserts the exact chat_messages_bulk_delete command, payload, and { timeoutMs: null } request option.

positiveRows.claim: The exact UI error reported on the Pi comes from a single-message deletion that uses the specialized wrapper.
positiveRows.evidence: The timeline action shows "Could not delete the message." only when useDeleteMessage rejects, and useDeleteMessage delegates to chatCommandApi.bulkDeleteMessages.

positiveRows.claim: Existing generic durable storage mutations retain their no-deadline policy.
positiveRows.evidence: The focused storage-api regression suite passes alongside the specialized wrapper test.

contradictionRows.claim: The wrapper must not claim success before the server returns.
contradictionRows.evidence: The implementation still awaits and returns invokeTauri directly; it changes only the request deadline option.

contradictionRows.claim: The deletion payload and Rust command contract must remain unchanged.
contradictionRows.evidence: The regression asserts the existing chatId and messageIds payload, and no Rust or HTTP dispatch file changed.

contradictionRows.claim: The change must not remove finite deadlines globally.
contradictionRows.evidence: Only the specialized bulkDeleteMessages call supplies timeoutMs: null; existing generic read/default deadline coverage remains unchanged.

legacyDefaultRows.evidence: The existing invokeTauri bridge ignores remote request options for embedded IPC and the command payload is unchanged.

legacyDefaultRows.claim: All existing callers keep the same typed API.
legacyDefaultRows.evidence: bulkDeleteMessages retains its chatId and messageIds signature and return type.

untestedRows: A real destructive message deletion was not repeated after deployment because verification must not modify the user's existing conversations.

ownedFacts.description: The Pi was running matching server and web images for main commit b555cf9ab594cdb10582b405ceee1f874977ef85 when the failure was diagnosed.
ownedFacts.evidence: The Pi checkout HEAD and both Docker OCI revision labels matched.

ownedFacts.description: Live Pi logs showed chat_messages_bulk_delete starting without a completion while subsequent storage operations took roughly 29 to 35 seconds.
ownedFacts.evidence: Read-only de-koi-server log inspection captured the stalled command starts and nearby slow completed storage calls.

ownedFacts.description: The generic storage mutation wrappers already opt out of the browser deadline, but the specialized chat command wrapper did not.
ownedFacts.evidence: Direct comparison of storage-api.ts and chat-command-api.ts on the deployed revision showed the missing request option.

userActionCopy.description: Message deletion remains destructive. Export any conversation that must be recoverable before deleting its messages.
userActionCopy.source: Use the conversation export action before confirming deletion.
userActionCopy.destination: A user-selected folder outside De-Koi's application data directory.
userActionCopy.action: Confirm the exported conversation file exists at the selected destination before deleting irreplaceable messages.

manualBlockers.item: Post-merge destructive message deletion on the live Pi
manualBlockers.reason: The focused regression proves the transport contract, and exact merged image, health, container, and mount state can be verified without deleting a real user message.

verification.baselineEvidence: The new focused test failed before the wrapper supplied a request option. After the one-line fix, the chat-command and generic storage wrapper suites passed 8 tests; typecheck, architecture checks, formatting, and the full repository check passed.

notes: The user explicitly authorized PR creation, merge to main, and Pi deployment.
No live user messages will be deleted as part of deployment verification.
